title: GS Caltex Foundation Presents 'True People Award' to 12, Including Citizens Who Subdued Knife-Wielding Assailant - 아시아경제

GS Caltex Foundation Presents 'True People Award' to 12, Including Citizens Who Subdued Knife-Wielding Assailant The GS Caltex Foundation, chaired by Huh Jin-soo, presented its True Person Award to 12 individuals and groups, including citizens who subdued an armed assailant with their bare hands and a dentist who has provided free treatment for nearly 30 years. Award recipients pose for a commemorative photo at the 2026 GS Caltex True Person Award ceremony held at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, on the 28th. GS Caltex Foundation The foundation said on October 29 that it held the 2026 GS Caltex True Person Award ceremony at GS Tower in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, on October 28, presenting plaques and prize money to eight recipients in the Heroism category, three in the Good Deeds category, and one organization. Established in 2020, the award recognizes and encourages people who risk their lives to save others or consistently do good for their neighbors. According to the foundation, the Heroism category recipients included Na Hyeonjun, Shin Insu, Shin Junghyun, Lee Hyeonmin and Kim Jungyeon, who subdued a person rampaging with knives tied to both hands at a commercial building in Guwol-dong, Namdong-gu, Incheon, on October 13. They pursued the assailant and threw chairs to block his way in, then joined together to restrain him after he fell and remove the knives, preventing further harm. Also among the recipients were Ko Yeongu, a sergeant with the Army’s 22nd Infantry Division, who rescued a 13-year-old swept away by waves at a beach in Geojin-eup, Goseong-gun, Gangwon Province, on July 19, when a heavy rain advisory was in effect; and Lee Donggyu, an employee of the Jeonju Facilities Management Corporation, who rescued a father and daughter being swept out to sea by taking them onto his surfboard at Hamdeok Beach on Jeju Island on September 15. Kim Sewung was also recognized for helping apprehend a suspect to the end despite being stabbed while pursuing the assailant in a robbery at a commercial building in Geumho-dong, Seo-gu, Gwangju, on February 2, despite being visually impaired. In the Good Deeds category, the award went to Park Yungyu, a dentist in Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province, who has provided free treatment for nearly 30 years in medically underserved areas at home and abroad after losing one leg in a train accident; and Nanumnurihoe, a residents’ group in Gayang-dong, Gangseo-gu, Seoul, which has prepared breakfasts for children in need and delivered side dishes to vulnerable people since 1996. Lee Wonsuk, a conductor who has helped young people with disabilities and from low-income families become performers in the Beautiful Mind Orchestra, Korea’s first integrated orchestra for musicians with and without disabilities, and Lee Bokdan, who has delivered lunchboxes and side dishes to older adults living alone and others every weekday for more than 20 years, also received awards. A foundation representative said, “The spirit of those who risk their lives to save others and of those who have reached out to their neighbors over many years is a pillar of our society. We will continue to seek out and support people who dedicate themselves to others.” © The Asia Business Daily. All rights reserved. Unauthorized AI training and use prohibited. GS Shop Expands Private-Brand Products, Targets Fashion, Bedding and Beauty GS Shop is expanding new private-brand (PB) products in key categories, including fashion, home and living, and beauty, to strengthen the competitiveness of its exclusive products. GS Shop said on October 29 that it will introduce “Peach-Brushed Multiwear,” a winter release from its underwear brand UBGS, on TV home shopping on October 30. The collection consists of three tops with built-in bra cups and three bottoms, including winter thermal underwear and long pants. GS Shop is launching “Peach-Brushed Multiwear” as part of the fall/winter line from its in-house underwear brand UBGS. GS Shop On the same day, GS Shop will also air the second broadcast of “Boilable 100% Wool Bedding Set” from its bedding brand Heriden. Developed with input from around 3,000 customers, the product sold out during its first broadcast, recording 920 million won in orders. Its in-house beauty brand Byu will launch five types of “Skin Fit Mask Pack” on its mobile app, made with biodegradable fabric that has received vegan certification. GS Shop’s private brands are also delivering sales results. UBGS, launched last May, has sold 230,000 pieces of underwear and surpassed 2 billion won in cumulative orders. Byu, meanwhile, had more than 70,000 cumulative ordering customers through the third quarter of this year. “The strength of private brands is that they can offer differentiated exclusive products by incorporating customers’ actual purchasing data and feedback from the product-planning stage,” said Lee Yoonji, manager of GS Shop’s Casual Underwear Team. “We will continue to offer products tailored to customer demand across a range of categories and strengthen the competitiveness of our private brands.” © The Asia Business Daily. Georgia Southern University researchers can now compete for federal funding, including Department of Defense funding that requires strict cybersecurity protections, after the university’s Talon Secure virtual environment earned Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level 2 certification. With Talon Secure certified, Georgia Southern faculty can pursue larger grants, support current Department of Defense-funded projects and join defense companies as research partners or subcontractors. Inside Talon Secure, researchers can store and work with government information that is unclassified but still must be safeguarded, such as technical data tied to defense programs. The certification confirms the system meets federal requirements for protecting that information. “Protecting sensitive research isn’t a box we check, it’s a standard we hold ourselves to every day,” said Georgia Southern Vice President for Research and Innovation David Weindorf, Ph.D. “This certification opens the door for our faculty to compete for consequential defense research, and it tells our federal partners they can bring that work to Georgia Southern with confidence.” Talon Secure was reviewed by a Certified Third-Party Assessor Organization and earned a perfect score, with no deficiencies in any of the 14 security categories tested. Several Georgia Southern departments collaborated to prepare for the audit, including the Office of Research Integrity, Research Security and Export Controls and Information Technology Services. Janny Crespo-Grow, Ph.D., director of the Office of Research Integrity, said the assessor described Georgia Southern’s performance as “the standard for what we should see in our assessments.” Crespo-Grow, part of the Office of Research Integrity, specifically credited Chief Information Security Officer Nic Carroll and his team, who “took point” in preparation. Carroll highlighted the cross-divisional collaboration behind the audit. “Preparing for the audit meant bringing together people from the Office of Research and Innovation, IT, information security and compliance to answer one honest question: ‘Does what we actually do every day match what our written procedures say we do?’” he said. He added assessors tested 110 security controls against 320 assessment objectives. “The assessment confirmed our protections are followed in practice, not just written down, and that is what gives our researchers an environment they can trust,” Carroll said.

title: PC-12 Training Device Installed at Air Bravo in One-G’s Canada Debut - Aviation International News
content: Air charter operator Air Bravo can now train PC-12 pilots at its facility in Thunder Bay, Ontario, where One-G Simulation has installed a Swiss12 advanced aviation training device (AATD) modeled on the turboprop single. The Swiss12 device received its initial FAA letter of authorization as an AATD in 2017. This installation is the Seattle company’s first in Canada. Air Bravo has ordered a second device for the Cessna 408 SkyCourier; in 2025, the operator took the first SkyCourier delivered in Canada. One-G matched the device to the PC-12s that Air Bravo flies, down to their installed avionics. Pilots can use the AATD for procedures, systems management, and abnormal and emergency scenarios, subject to the operator’s training requirements and applicable regulatory approvals, including those from Transport Canada. Hardware includes aerodynamically-driven force-feedback yokes, linked rudder pedals with toe brakes, a fully functional overhead panel, a crew alerting system (CAS) panel, and visuals projected onto a curved screen. From One-G’s instructor operator station, instructors set aircraft position, weather, and system failures. “A PC-12 operator shouldn’t have to send pilots out of province for every recurrent event,” said One-G founder and CEO Xylon Saltzman. “Because we build the hardware and software ourselves, we could match this device to Air Bravo’s aircraft and put that training in their own hangar.”

title: Benny G’s Mom, a Breast Cancer Survivor, Emotionally Introduces Him to the Grand Ole Opry Stage on Opry Goes Pink Night - American Songwriter
content: Benny G got a very special introduction to the Grand Ole Opry stage. The singer performed during Opry Goes pink, an annual concert put on in partnership with Susan G. Komen amid Breast Cancer Awareness month. Ahead of Benny’s performance, Opry host Kelly Sutton stepped aside to allow the singer’s mom, breast cancer survivor Ally Goldsmith, to introduce her son. “Five years ago I was diagnosed at the age of 43 with metastatic breast cancer,” Goldsmith began. She went on to shout out the doctors who cared for her amid her illness, before turning the focus to her son. “I believe that every single soul is an entire universe,” she said. “So naturally, there is no greater blessing in my life than the three incredible lights that I refer to as my children.” Goldsmith went to reveal how Benny comforted her during the height of her illness. “When I was ill, he would sit at the edge of my bed with his acoustic guitar and we would sing songs together by many of the artists that performed on this legendary stage,” she said. “It was music and my unwavering faith that gave me both comfort and strength during such a challenging time.” “I want to thank the Grand Ole Opry for shining a bright pink light on this awful disease and also giving me the honor of introducing this next performer,” Goldsmith continued. “This truly is our full circle moment. So with all the joy in my heart, which I refer to is nachas, ladies and gentlemen, let’s give a Grand Ole Opry welcome to my son, Benny G.” “Love you mom, first of all,” he said. “This first song I’m going to play you guys is actually inspired by my mom and her perseverance and faith when she had cancer… It’s called ‘Heaven Knows We Just Keep Dancing Through It All,’ ’cause that’s what life’s about, really.” Next, Benny performed “In the Now,” a song he co-wrote with his sister, Ella Goldsmith. The 19-year-old performer concluded his set by welcoming Briley King back out onto the stage. The pair performed a cover of Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell’s “Ain’t No Mountain High Enough.” Benny wasn’t the only star on hand for the special Opry show. Deana Carter opened up the night, and was followed by sets from Mackenzie Carpenter and Megan Moroney. Additionally, Jillian Cardarelli made her Grand Ole Opry debut. Audience members were also treated to solo sets by both King and Mandy Barnett.

title: "I will definitely beat my older sister when I face her." GS Caltex's Park Eun-bin, the youngest daughter of an Olympic volleyball national team player and a mother, writes V-League history as the first "three sisters selected in the 1st round" - 스타뉴스
content:
"I really want to win when I meet my older sister." The youngest daughter of a father who is a wrestling Asian Games medalist and a mother who is a former Olympic volleyball national team player entered the professional stage following in her sisters' footsteps. Park Eun-bin (18), an outside hitter from Sunmyung Girls' High School, completed a historic record as the first set of three sisters to all be selected in the 1st round of the rookie draft in V-League history. Park Eun-bin was selected by GS Caltex with the 7th overall pick in the 1st round at the 2026~2027 Korea Volleyball Federation (KOVO) Women's Rookie Draft held on the 28th at the Mayfield Hotel in Gangseo-gu, Seoul. With this, Park Eun-bin became a 1st-round pick in professional volleyball alongside her eldest sister Park Eun-seo (23) and second sister Park Eun-ji (22). Park Eun-seo was selected by Pepper Savings Bank AI Peppers with the 2nd overall pick in the 1st round of the rookie draft for the 2021~2022 season. The following year, setter Park Eun-ji joined KGC Ginseng Corporation (now Cheongguangjang) as the 4th overall pick in the 1st round of the 2022~2023 season. Currently, Park Eun-seo plays for SOOP Supers, and Park Eun-ji plays for the Pohang City Sports Council volleyball team. It is the first time since the launch of the V-League that three sisters have each received the honor of being selected in the 1st round. The family's background is also unique. Their father, Mr. Park Woo, is a bronze medalist in the Greco-Roman 97kg class at wrestling at the 1998 Bangkok Asian Games. Their mother, Eo Yeon-soon, served as a women's volleyball national team player at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics and the 2000 Sydney Olympics. She played as an outside hitter for Korea Expressway Corporation and currently serves as a KOVO referee committee member. Meeting the press immediately after the draft, Park Eun-bin said, "I am still lacking in many ways, but I am truly grateful to GS Caltex for picking me so early in the 1st round," adding, "Since I am the last athlete in my family, my family members have supported me a lot and also worried about me. But it seems things turned out well, which is fortunate," smiling. Regarding the record of being the first among three sisters, she expressed joy, saying, "I heard a lot of such stories while participating in the draft. It is wonderful that all three of us could go to the 1st round." She then expressed gratitude, stating, "My eldest sister told me not to be nervous and to do well. My younger sister also supported me. My mother often gave advice when I encountered difficult parts or unknown things while playing volleyball." Interestingly, Park Eun-bin did not dream of being an attacker from the beginning. Rather, she wanted to become a setter like her second sister Park Eun-ji. Park Eun-bin said, "Actually, I wanted to be a setter, but because my height grew rapidly, I automatically became an attacker," adding, "I grew 10cm per year for three years when I was young. Now it seems good that I became an attacker." The period of substantial growth was during her second year of high school. Park Eun-bin reflected, "As I entered my second year, many of the attacking sisters graduated. I had more opportunities to hit the ball, and by approaching games with a sense of responsibility, I think I was able to grow a bit more." GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek (49) also paid attention to her growth trend. The coach said, "Park Eun-bin has good attacking power and decent physical conditions. I think her skills have grown significantly since her second year," adding, "She is currently a bit lacking compared to her sister, but there is definitely the potential for her to do better than her sister." However, he placed more weight on long-term development rather than immediate performance. The coach explained, "I heard that she has a slight injury in her shoulder area. I think it is something that can be managed sufficiently," adding, "Rather than using her immediately, I plan to take time to gradually build up her body and develop her." GS Caltex also secured Oh Hae-sol (18), an outside hitter from Sunmyung Girls' High School, with the 8th overall pick in the 2nd round on this day. Two classmates will begin their professional careers together at GS Caltex, which won the women's championship finals last year. The coach expressed satisfaction, saying, "Both players were high up on our selection list." Specifically regarding Oh Hae-sol, he explained, "She was a player I viewed very favorably in her first year of high school. However, she underwent surgery for an ACL injury in her second year and had a one-year gap. I judged that Park Eun-bin is currently slightly better in terms of game performance, so I chose her first." Park Eun-bin has another dream to achieve in the professional league. That is to face off against her sisters on the same court. She stated, "There is an age difference with Eun-seo sister, so I have never stood on the same court with her. My sisters were born in consecutive years, so I often saw them saying they would win every time they played each other. I was disappointed that I could not do that, but now I can," declaring her determination to "definitely want to win when I meet my sisters." <© STARNEWS. All rights reserved. title: Freddy Carrick-Smith’s 12th in Sölden Makes British GS History - Ski Racing Media
content: Freddy Carrick-Smith scored his first World Cup points in Sölden, finishing 12th in the 2026/27 men’s season-opening giant slalom. Lucas Pinheiro Braathen won the race with his fourth straight elite giant slalom victory. Carrick-Smith’s result gave Britain its first men’s World Cup GS top 30 since March 2022. Carrick-Smith’s twin brother Zak and elder brother Luca watched from the finish area. His mother, four-time British Olympian Emma Carrick-Anderson, remains his technician and watched from the wings. Freddy’s father, Phil Smith, remains watched from the top. Freddy heard him last before pushing out of the Rettenbach start gate. This wasn’t just Freddy’s first World Cup points result. It also put Britain back on the giant slalom map. His family has worked nearly 20 years for this moment. Speaking exclusively with the Skiing Is Believing podcast less than 24 hours after the race, Carrick-Smith said, “The whole family was there … and we were over the moon after the second run.” This was only Carrick-Smith’s fifth World Cup start and second in Sölden. He made his World Cup debut there 12 months earlier. He finished 54th after the first run, more than 1.6 seconds outside the top 30. Carrick-Smith started with bib 46 and tied Norway’s Hans Grahl-Madsen for 21st after Run 1. “When I saw the 21st on the screen, I was happy and actually snapped my pole while celebrating,” he said. He then produced the fifth-fastest second run and climbed nine places. The course had one speed trap before the final flat, measuring the speed racers carried into the closing stretch. Carrick-Smith posted the fastest reading in Run 1 at 82.20 km/h. His 80.20 km/h in Run 2 ranked second. Carrick-Smith summed up what the result meant to him: “If you don’t enjoy the journey, you’re not going to enjoy the result.” Jeremy Palmer-Tomkinson’s ninth-place finish in Méribel, France, on March 10, 1968, remains Britain’s best men’s World Cup GS result. Carrick-Smith’s 12th was the country’s best in the discipline since then. Charlie Raposo had Britain’s last men’s World Cup GS top 30 before Sölden. He finished 27th in Kranjska Gora on March 12, 2022, then placed 16th the next day. Raposo was in Sölden on Sunday and told Ski Racing Media, “I’m very glad that someone has come along and taken that.” Raposo also praised Carrick-Smith’s skiing and focus between runs: “It was super fun to watch. He was calm, super dialed and super focused between runs so super excited for him.” Carrick-Smith also became the first British man to score World Cup points in Sölden. Chemmy Alcott remains Britain’s top finisher there, placing 10th in 2008. This result means the Carrick-Smith family’s schedule for late November and December now looks a little different. Freddy’s 12th-place finish opened a start opportunity for Zak at the men’s World Cup giant slalom in Copper Mountain, Colorado, on Nov. 29. Before then, Freddy might make his World Cup slalom debut in Levi, Finland, on Nov. 15. Dave Ryding’s retirement after the 2026 Olympic Winter Games could create an opening alongside slalom specialists Laurie Taylor and Billy Major. Freddy and Zak turn 20 in February. The Sölden result gives Freddy a chance, with limited pressure, to leave his footprint in the snow. It could also put two Carrick-Smith brothers on a World Cup start list together. The next generation of British athletes is stepping up to the top level. Whether it’s Freddy, Luca or Zak, the Carrick-Smith name on the World Cup results sheet is one fans may have to get used to. The Skiing Is Believing podcast also featured Carrick-Smith in its Sölden review show. Listen below on Spotify or YouTube, with special guests Britt Janyk and William St-Germain.                                        My Trusted Source Goldman Sachs has built much of its recent reputation on trading and financing for institutional clients, and the third-quarter report showed how heavily that business can swing the overall result. According to the firm's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, net revenues were about eighteen point six eight billion dollars, up about twenty-three percent from the third quarter a year earlier, though about eight percent below the exceptionally strong second quarter. The company is one of the names followed closely in our Financial Stocks section. Net earnings came in at about five point two nine billion dollars, equal to seventeen dollars and one cent per diluted share, against twelve dollars and twenty-five cents a year earlier and twenty dollars and ninety-eight cents in the second quarter. On the index front, Goldman Sachs is part of the [Dow Jones Industrial Average], S&P 500, NYSE Composite and Russell 1000, which keeps the stock on the radar of index-linked funds. The annualized earnings rate on common equity was about eighteen point seven percent for the quarter and about twenty point seven percent for the first nine months of the year. The release matters beyond the headline because it exposes several moving parts at once: an equities desk that grew at a pace few competitors matched, a deal backlog that eased, a consumer-finance unit that is being wound down, and a capital ratio that moved lower as the firm continued to retire shares. This article lays out each of those pieces using the filing and published coverage. The release was issued earlier this month, and no later company-specific filing of comparable weight has appeared since. The filing lists net revenues of about eighteen point six eight billion dollars for the quarter and about fifty-six point two four billion dollars for the first nine months. Net earnings were about five point two nine billion dollars for the quarter and about seventeen point five five billion dollars year to date. Diluted earnings per share were seventeen dollars and one cent, and nine-month per-share earnings were fifty-five dollars and fifty-six cents. The sequential decline from the second quarter is worth noting. Revenue fell about eight percent and per-share earnings dropped from twenty dollars and ninety-eight cents to seventeen dollars and one cent, which shows that the second quarter set a high bar. Year over year, however, the comparison is strongly positive, with per-share earnings about thirty-nine percent higher. Book value per share was about three hundred seventy-two dollars and sixty-four cents, up about one point four percent during the quarter and about four point two percent so far this year. That growth is more modest than the earnings growth because the firm distributed a large amount of capital through dividends and share retirement. The efficiency ratio for the first nine months was about fifty-nine point four percent, meaning that operating costs consumed a little under sixty cents of each revenue dollar. The firm's filing marks several capital figures as preliminary, so final numbers could differ slightly when the regulatory filings are completed. Equities was the single largest revenue line in the report, at about six point four four billion dollars. The filing attributes the increase to financing and intermediation, with derivatives singled out. Financing refers to services such as prime brokerage and margin lending that the firm provides to hedge funds and other clients, while intermediation covers market making in cash stocks and derivatives. The size of the jump stands out against the rest of the report. Fixed-rate, currency and commodity trading revenue, which the firm reports as FICC, was about three point four seven billion dollars, roughly flat from a year earlier. In other words, the whole firm-wide improvement in trading came from one side of the house. Revenue of this type tends to follow client activity. Periods of rapid price movement, heavy options volume and growing hedge fund balances generally lift equity financing revenue. The same conditions helped JPMorgan Chase, which reported a sharp equities gain of its own, and Charles Schwab, which reported higher trading revenue from retail clients. The filing does not provide forward guidance for the line. Because financing revenue depends on client balance sheets and market volatility, it may not repeat at the same scale in later quarters, a point that is often raised when Wall Street research desks compare the second and third quarter figures. Fees from advisory work and from underwriting stock and debt were about three point two two billion dollars, up about twenty-one percent from a year earlier. According to the filing, the rise was led by higher advisory revenue and higher equity underwriting revenue. Those two lines are closely tied to completed mergers and to new share sales, both of which have been more active this year. The filing also notes that the backlog of announced but not yet completed work declined from the end of the second quarter and edged lower versus the end of last year. The firm does not publish a dollar figure for the backlog in the release, so the size of the decline cannot be stated. A smaller backlog can mean that more transactions closed during the period, which boosts current revenue but leaves fewer deals waiting to convert later. The Global Banking and Markets segment, which houses advisory, underwriting and trading, reported net revenues of about thirteen point four six billion dollars, up about thirty-two percent year over year but down about thirteen percent from the second quarter. For the firm, advisory strength has a double effect. It lifts revenue directly and it supports the standing of the franchise with corporate clients who may also use its trading and financing services. For the coming quarters, the open question is whether new announcements refill the backlog at the same pace that completions drain it. Asset and Wealth Management produced net revenues of about five point zero five billion dollars, up about fourteen percent from a year earlier and about ten percent from the second quarter. The filing attributes the increase mainly to higher management fees and incentive fees. Management fees rise when client assets grow, either through market gains or through new money, and incentive fees are paid when funds beat their performance hurdles. The latter can be lumpy, which is why this segment's revenue can vary more than the headline growth rate implies. Even so, the sequential increase indicates that the fee base was larger during the quarter than it was in the second quarter. The firm has been working to increase the share of revenue that comes from fee-based activities rather than from trading, a goal that executives have described at earlier events as a way to make results steadier. At about five billion dollars, the segment contributed roughly twenty-seven percent of total net revenues in the quarter, with the remainder coming mainly from Global Banking and Markets. The filing does not break out the sources of incentive fees or the amount of client inflows in the portions reviewed for this article, so those details are not covered here. Readers who want them can consult the full release and the supplemental materials on the company's website. Platform Solutions, the unit that includes the firm's consumer-facing credit card relationships, reported net revenues of about one hundred seventy million dollars, down about seventy-two percent from a year earlier. The filing says the decline reflects markdowns on the Apple Card loan portfolio. Goldman Sachs has been moving away from consumer lending, and the Apple Card arrangement has been the largest remaining piece of that business. A markdown means the carrying value of the loans was reduced, a step that usually accompanies a planned transfer or a change in the expected value of the portfolio. The filing as summarized for this article does not detail the acquirer or the timetable of any transfer, so those points are left out. The unit is small relative to the overall firm. At about one hundred seventy million dollars, it accounted for under one percent of third-quarter net revenues. Even so, the decline detracts from the comparison with last year and illustrates a theme that has run through the firm's recent reports: the effort to simplify the business and concentrate on institutional clients and wealth management. For stock owners, the importance of this line lies less in its size than in the signal about strategy. Further adjustments are possible, and the amounts will depend on how the transition of the portfolio proceeds. Operating expenses were about eleven point three one billion dollars, up about twenty percent from a year earlier and down about three percent from the second quarter. Expense growth of twenty percent is slightly below the twenty-three percent increase in revenue, so the quarter showed modest operating leverage on a year-over-year basis. Compensation is the largest component of costs at a firm like Goldman Sachs, and it tends to rise and fall with revenue. When trading and advisory revenue climb, bonus accruals follow. That is why the cost line moved up even though management has talked about efficiency. The provision for credit losses was about three hundred sixty-eight million dollars, which the filing says was mostly related to impairments in the wholesale loan portfolio. The amount is small relative to the revenue base, but wholesale impairments are watched closely across the sector because they relate to lending to corporations and to specialized finance borrowers. The effective tax rate for the first nine months was about twenty point four percent. A change in that rate can move per-share earnings noticeably, so market participants usually look at it alongside the pre-tax figures. The filing gives no specific explanation for the rate beyond the nine-month calculation, and no change was flagged for the fourth quarter. The standardized common equity tier one ratio was an estimated twelve point four percent, down from twelve point nine percent at the end of the second quarter. Under the advanced approach, the ratio was thirteen point six percent and unchanged. The standardized figure is the one that typically binds for large U.S. banks, so the half-point decline attracted attention. During the quarter the firm retired about three billion dollars of its stock, which amounts to roughly two point nine million shares at an average price of about one thousand forty-eight dollars and seventy-three cents. It also paid about one point four nine billion dollars in dividends. Together those distributions are a large share of quarterly net earnings, and they help explain why the capital ratio edged lower even in a strong quarter. Part of the ratio's decline can also come from growth in exposure-weighted assets, which rise when trading and financing balances expand. The equities surge likely required more balance-sheet capacity, though the filing does not itself draw that link in the sections reviewed. The firm said its board declared a quarterly dividend of five dollars per share, payable on December thirtieth. A steady dividend and large share retirement program indicate confidence in capital strength, but regulators' capital requirements remain a constraint that management has to manage. Goldman Sachs reported its equities revenue growth at about seventy-two percent. JPMorgan Chase, with a much bigger consumer and commercial base, reported equities growth of about forty-nine percent. The gap shows how much more of Goldman Sachs's total is tied to institutional trading, which makes its results more sensitive to market conditions. On deal-making, both firms reported a rise in advisory activity, though Goldman Sachs's backlog commentary was cautious. Both also highlighted wholesale credit as an area to watch. Where they differ most is in the breadth of the earnings base. JPMorgan's consumer, card and payments businesses offer revenue that moves more gradually, while Goldman Sachs leans on trading, advisory and fee-based asset management. Charles Schwab, which operates a retail brokerage and banking platform, reported record client asset gathering in the same season, a reminder that heavy market participation helps both Wall Street trading desks and retail-facing platforms, although through different revenue lines. Price-level commentary is outside the scope of this article, but it is fair to say that the earnings pattern of the group has been uneven from one quarter to the next, and that the third-quarter results at Goldman Sachs came after a stronger second quarter. Whether the trading cycle stays elevated is the main unknown. Several items from the filing are likely to remain in view. The first is the pace of equities revenue, which was exceptionally high and may normalize. The second is the advisory backlog, which declined during the quarter. The third is the capital ratio, given the large distributions and the possibility of changes to regulatory requirements. A fourth item is the Platform Solutions transition. The Apple Card markdowns indicate that the consumer business is still working through the end of its life cycle inside the firm, and additional adjustments could follow. A fifth is expense discipline, since compensation costs rose alongside revenue. The next quarterly report will provide the next full set of data. Before then, executives often speak at industry conferences and may comment on deal activity and client behavior. Those comments are not guidance in the formal sense and should be treated as management perspective at a point in time. Nothing in this article is a view on how the stock or the business will perform. The purpose is to record what the company reported and to identify the factors that frame the discussion, so that the figures can be read in context. title: BMW F 450 GS Trophy Edition: Big GS Energy, A Few Growing Pains - Man's World India
content: The smallest GS has grown up, gained a second cylinder, and learned to operate its own clutch. But is that enough to justify its premium price tag? For a long time, the G 310 GS was the cheapest way into the GS family in India. The F 450 GS replaces it, and it is a different kind of motorcycle. It has a new 420cc parallel twin, and the top variant, the Trophy Edition, also gets the Easy Ride Clutch. BMW launched the Trophy at ₹5.30 lakh ex-showroom in April. In September, the price went up by ₹30,000, so it now costs ₹5.60 lakh. I have spent some time with it, and I mostly like it. The engine is the one part I am still trying to figure out. I like the design. It reminds me of the older GS siblings, with the beak, the flyline and the tall stance. The X-shaped headlamp comes from the R 1300 GS, and the Trophy's Racing Blue with red and white accents suits it well. It also gets you a lot of attention. A lot of people asked me what bike it is, and how much it costs. The answer to that is ₹5.60 lakh ex-showroom. It looks heavy, but it doesn't feel heavy at all. BMW says the kerb weight is 178 kg, and the bike is very well balanced. I am 183 cm tall, and I was able to flat-foot it on the 845 mm seat. It is a fairly large motorcycle, though. In traffic, you have to be careful while manoeuvring it in tight spaces. The Trophy gets BMW's Easy Ride Clutch, or ERC. It is a centrifugal clutch that engages after roughly 2,500 to 2,700 rpm, so you can move off and come to a stop without using the clutch lever. You still change gears yourself, and the Trophy also gets a quickshifter. It takes some time to get used to. The feeling of not using the clutch is a bit uncanny at first. But it works well, and the bike doesn't stall. And if you don't want to leave it to the system, you can take over manual control with the lever at any time. The suspension is really good. The Trophy gets the sport setup, which means a 43 mm KYB upside-down fork with adjustable compression and rebound, and a rear monoshock with travel-dependent damping. Both ends have 180 mm of travel. It is slightly on the stiffer side, and I like it that way. Heavier riders may like it even more. The 420cc parallel twin makes 48 hp at 8,750 rpm and 43 Nm at 6,750 rpm. BMW says 80 per cent of that torque is available from 3,000 rpm, and the engine does have great pull. It stays very refined till about 80 to 90 kmph. Once you start pushing it, you can feel the engine working. I was able to push it past 120 kmph, but it felt a little stressed at that point. The character is the part I find hard to describe. It is not very refined, even though it is a twin and it carries a BMW badge. But it is also not as characterful or as frantic as the 390 Adventure. It sits somewhere in a strange, boring middle. BMW has gone with an unusual 135-degree crank on this engine. The idea is to keep vibrations in check and give it a throaty sound, but I would not call the result either refined or exciting. The saddle is quite nice, for both the rider and the pillion. The brakes are good and bitey, with a 310 mm disc at the front. This is the part I find bizarre. At ₹5.60 lakh ex-showroom, the bike gets a 6.5-inch TFT, riding modes that change the throttle response, and heated grips as standard. But there is no Hill Hold Control and no cruise control. Without Hill Hold Control, the bike can roll back when you stop on a slope, and there is no parking brake either. Reviewers have also found that leaving the bike in gear on an incline doesn't reliably hold it in place. That feels like an odd gap on a bike that is built to make starting and stopping easier. Cruise control is not offered even as an optional extra, which is a miss on a bike that is meant for long distances. There is a lot to like here. The design, the balance, the suspension, the saddle and the brakes are all good, and the ERC works well once you get used to it. The engine is where it doesn't quite make up its mind. It pulls well and stays refined in the first half of its range, but it is not as smooth as I would expect from a BMW twin, and it is not as exciting as the 390 Adventure. At ₹5.60 lakh ex-showroom, that is hard to overlook, and the missing Hill Hold Control and cruise control make it harder. If you want a light, good-looking GS that is comfortable for two, this does the job well. Just know what you are getting with the engine.

title: GS Affiliate Energy Materials Suspends Operations Amid Financial Woes, Pursues Sale - 아시아경제

GS Affiliate Energy Materials Suspends Operations Amid Financial Woes, Pursues Sale GS E&C's waste battery recycling subsidiary Energy Materials has halted operations at its factory amid financial difficulties. Losses have mounted due to difficulties securing raw materials and falling prices for recovered metals, and the company is pursuing a sale after undertaking restructuring measures, including offering voluntary retirement. Energy Materials, a secondary battery recycling company in Pohang, North Gyeongsang Province. Yonhap News Agency According to industry sources, Energy Materials suspended operations at its factory in Pohang, North Gyeongsang Province, on October 28. It is also offering voluntary retirement to its more than 130 employees. Founded in October 2020, Energy Materials has extracted battery metals, including lithium, nickel, cobalt, and manganese, from black powder, a black substance obtained by shredding and heat-treating waste batteries. Despite large-scale investment in facilities, the factory's operating rate remained at around 30%. Because of the time lag between the adoption of electric vehicles and the eventual disposal of their batteries, the company could not secure enough feedstock for processing. The decline in selling prices for recovered metals further worsened profitability. With the factory operating at a low rate, the company continued to bear fixed costs for facilities and personnel, and its cumulative losses reached about 170 billion won. The company pursued cost reductions, workforce efficiency measures, diversification of raw-material suppliers and product buyers, and efforts to attract new investors, but was unable to overcome its financial difficulties. Challenges in the battery recycling industry are also continuing overseas. title: Base Editing Pinpoints Exon 7 Knockout for High-Yield CHO Antibody Production - Bioengineer.org
content: Base Editing Pinpoints Exon 7 Knockout for High-Yield CHO Antibody Production Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells dominate the manufacturing of recombinant therapeutic proteins, and the glutamine synthetase (GS) selection system is one of the most widely used tools for building production cell lines. Yet two commercial GS-deficient CHO platforms, ATCC CHO-K1 and Merck’s CHOZN, behave very differently in the hands of cell-line engineers, and researchers have now traced part of that divergence to a surprisingly simple variable: exactly where along the GS gene a premature stop codon lands. A new study published in Bioresources and Bioprocessing systematically introduced stop mutations into each of the six coding exons of the Glul gene using cytosine base editing and found that the position of the premature termination codon (PTC) strongly determines whether the knockout is complete, how the cells respond to stress, and how much antibody they ultimately produce. The two commercial lines carry different frameshift mutations in Glul. ATCC CHO-K1, the first subclone derived from parental CHO-ori cells, harbors a 26-base-pair deletion in exon 2, while CHOZN cells were generated with zinc finger nucleases that created a 10-base-pair deletion and a 1-base-pair substitution in exon 6. Both mutations introduce frameshifts, and both lines show little or no detectable GS protein by Western blot. But when the researchers measured GS messenger RNA, they found substantial residual transcripts in both lines, showing that the frameshifts do not abolish transcription. The apparent loss of GS protein reflects a post-transcriptional block rather than transcript elimination, a distinction the authors argue should caution anyone treating residual mRNA as a proxy for residual enzyme activity. The behavioral contrast between the two platforms was striking. In glutamine-free medium, CHOZN cells were markedly more sensitive to glutamine deprivation, while ATCC CHO-K1 cells sustained relatively active proliferation even without the amino acid. Under methionine sulfoximine (MSX) selection, the inhibitor used in GS-based screening, both lines proliferated more slowly. Profiling of stress-response markers, including Atf4, Ddit3, and Ppp1r15a, revealed that CHOZN mounted a substantially amplified integrated stress response under deprivation, co-inducing residual GS transcripts with the stress genes, whereas ATCC CHO-K1 was essentially unresponsive, with neither GS transcript nor stress markers changing appreciably with glutamine status. The authors suggest this divergent stress engagement, rather than residual transcript abundance itself, may contribute to the different glutamine sensitivities. To test whether PTC position matters in a controlled setting, the team turned to a cytosine base editor, CBE4max-SpRY, which converts cytosine to thymine without creating double-strand DNA breaks. This matters because conventional nuclease editing with zinc finger nucleases, TALENs, or CRISPR/Cas9 relies on error-prone repair of double-strand breaks, producing heterogeneous mixtures of frameshift and in-frame alleles. In benchmarking experiments at exon 6, CRISPR/Cas9 achieved indel frequencies of up to 64 percent, three of seven TALEN pairs showed detectable activity with a maximum of 25.7 percent, and the ZFN pair reached 9.4 percent, but all of these double-strand-break strategies also generated in-frame indels at frequencies of 0.6 to 15.3 percent, edits that may fail to disrupt the reading frame at all. Base editing, by contrast, installs the intended stop codon directly, so the measured editing frequency reflects the desired outcome. Using sgRNAs designed against each coding exon, the researchers generated monoclonal lines carrying PTCs at six positions: Q27X in exon 2, W60X in exon 3, Q135X in exon 4, Q201X in exon 5, Q205X in exon 6, and R286X in exon 7. Residual GS transcript levels relative to the wild-type EK1 control ranged widely, from roughly 0.7-fold for the exon 2 line down to 0.03-fold for exon 4 and 0.04-fold for exon 7, with the exon 6 line at 0.39-fold. When the team depleted UPF1, a core component of the nonsense-mediated mRNA decay pathway, GS transcripts in the exon 4 and exon 7 lines rebounded dramatically, by approximately 19.2-fold and 12.8-fold respectively, providing functional evidence that UPF1-dependent decay is a major driver of the near-complete transcript depletion in those lines. Responses in the other lines were far weaker or absent. Protein measurements added a further layer of nuance. GS protein was undetectable in every PTC-edited line except the exon 6 line, despite substantial residual transcripts in several lines, particularly those edited at exons 2 and 3. The exon 6 line, uniquely, retained detectable GS protein and was the only edited line besides the wild-type parent that could proliferate in glutamine-free medium during serial-passage cultivation across a glutamine gradient of 0, 1, 2, and 6 millimolar. The authors conclude that transcript abundance alone is insufficient to predict knockout completeness, and that GS knockout cannot be regarded as a uniform binary state. The exon 7-edited line, designated E7, emerged as the standout. It showed complete functional GS deficiency, no detectable GS protein, and sustained high viability, retaining more than 90 percent viability throughout cultivation in glutamine-replete medium even though it grew more slowly and reached a lower peak viable cell density than the other edited lines. Because the exon 7 sgRNA sequence is fully conserved in the homologous GS1 locus on chromosome 1, the researchers also checked whether GS1 editing might explain the phenotype. Among three independent E7 clones, GS1 was homozygously edited in one, heterozygously edited in another, and unedited in the third, yet GS protein was undetectable in all three, and the clone with unedited GS1 showed growth and viability profiles comparable to its siblings. GS1, currently annotated as a noncoding pseudogene, showed no compensatory upregulation in most lines, leading the authors to conclude that GS1 editing is unlikely to be the principal determinant of the E7 phenotype, though they note a subtle contribution cannot be completely excluded. The production test used an anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody in 16-day fed-batch cultures of stable pools. Without MSX selection, the E7 pool yielded a final titer of 0.74 grams per liter at a cell-specific productivity of 3.7 picograms per cell per day, more than three times the productivity of the CHOZN control pool, which reached 0.39 grams per liter at 1.0 picogram per cell per day. With 5 micromolar MSX, the E7 titer rose 38 percent to 1.02 grams per liter with a productivity of 4.9 picograms per cell per day, 4.45-fold higher than the MSX-treated CHOZN pool. MSX produced no comparable improvement in the EK1 or CHOZN pools, which the authors attribute to host-dependent differences in selection stringency and pool enrichment rather than a productivity ceiling. All pools maintained high viability between 86 and 93 percent, with glucose between 1.06 and 5.02 grams per liter and lactate at basal levels of 0.00 to 1.09 grams per liter, indicating balanced metabolic profiles across the engineered lines. Transcriptomic analysis of the non-producing cell lines revealed graded remodeling: the ATCC CHO-K1 line showed the most extensive differential expression relative to the wild-type control, with 1,536 differentially expressed genes, while CHOZN was closest to the control with 304, and E7 was intermediate with 608. E7 showed marked downregulation of glutamate-ammonia ligase activity genes and nitrogen-assimilation pathways, a molecular hallmark of complete GS ablation that neither commercial line displayed. Compared with the exon 4 line, E7 also showed lower expression of genes involved in glutamine transport, nitrogen metabolism, proliferation, and basal ER-stress markers. The authors are careful to frame these as associations: the data do not establish that the expression changes were caused by the R286X position or that they drove the productivity advantage, and mechanisms such as transgene copy number and clonal composition were not directly examined. The study’s limitations are clearly stated. Most exon-specific comparisons used representative monoclonal lines, several growth and fed-batch experiments were single standardized runs on an industrial CDMO platform rather than biological replicates, and the production results require validation through independent fed-batch and clone-level studies. Targeted off-target sequencing of 13 predicted sites found editing only at the GS1 locus, RNA-seq-based variant analysis showed no significant increase in expressed SNPs or indels, and PCR confirmed elimination of residual editor plasmid sequences from all clonal lines, but the authors acknowledge that whole-genome sequencing would be needed to exclude rare variants. Within those bounds, the work delivers a defined, exon-resolved strategy: for laboratories building GS-deficient CHO hosts, the position of the stop codon is not a detail but a design parameter, and exon 7 stands out as a target that combines complete knockout with the manufacturing phenotype that cell-line developers prize. (2026). Base editing-mediated exon-specific knockout of glutamine synthetase generates a high-productivity CHO cell line for antibody manufacturing. title: The Goldman Sachs Group (NYSE:GS) CEO David Solomon Sells 12,000 Shares of Stock - MarketBeat

The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS - Get Free Report) CEO David Solomon sold 12,000 shares of the firm's stock in a transaction dated Tuesday, October 27th. The stock was sold at an average price of $910.72, for a total transaction of $10,928,640.00. Following the sale, the chief executive officer owned 159,180 shares of the company's stock, valued at $144,968,409.60. This trade represents a 7.01% decrease in their position. The transaction was disclosed in a legal filing with the SEC, which can be accessed through this link. Shares of The Goldman Sachs Group stock traded up $18.82 on Tuesday, reaching $912.10. 1,850,335 shares of the company traded hands, compared to its average volume of 2,218,525. The company has a 50 day moving average of $959.71 and a 200 day moving average of $958.88. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.82, a current ratio of 1.10 and a quick ratio of 0.63. The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. has a 52 week low of $754.00 and a 52 week high of $1,153.99. The firm has a market capitalization of $265.58 billion, a PE ratio of 13.11, a PEG ratio of 0.83 and a beta of 1.29. The Goldman Sachs Group (NYSE:GS - Get Free Report) last posted its quarterly earnings data on Tuesday, October 13th. The investment management company reported $17.01 EPS for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $12.86 by $4.15. The Goldman Sachs Group had a return on equity of 19.55% and a net margin of 15.77%. The business had revenue of $18.68 billion for the quarter, compared to the consensus estimate of $16.83 billion. title: 2027 Triumph Tiger 1200 Aims For The BMW GS's Do-Everything Crown - Jalopnik
content: If you want a motorcycle that does everything, you buy a BMW GS. It's such an easy choice, so rote that even BMW itself has felt the need to specialize its adventure lineup away from such perfectly omnicapable bikes. Now, though, another brand thinks it can hit the Bavarians where their hold is strongest. Triumph has revamped the Tiger 1200 lineup to hit BMW where it hurts, and the Brits have a solid shot of making a real mark. The Tiger 1200 line is still split into its four component models — GT Pro, Rally Pro, GT Explorer, and Rally Explorer — but Triumph has streamlined things between the four bikes to make their differences clearer. Every model now comes with a 19 inch front wheel and a 17 out back, and all four get trick self-lowering Showa suspension with 7.9 inches of travel front and rear — until you come to a stop, at which point the system drops the bike almost 1.2 inches. Triumph says the seat height, with a low seat installed and the self-lowering suspension active, can get as low as 31.1 inches at a stop. That's impressively low for a big adventure bike, and over an inch shorter than the competing R 1300 GS. On top of the trick suspension updates, Triumph has updated the Tiger's rider display — a new 7-inch display with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto now standard. There's also the updated 1,160cc three-cylinder engine with a redesigned cylinder head, new pistons, lighter intake and exhaust valves, and revised gear ratios for first, second, and third. The engine now makes 155.8 horsepower (up from 147 hp). Triumph also claims that the new Tiger 1200 has more torque down low, which improves slow-speed performance. If you're a bit confused by all the Tiger 1200's available variants, here's how Triumph differentiates them: GT bikes get cast wheels, while the Rally bikes get spokes. Rally bikes get an extra off-road ride mode and some engine protection. Explorer bikes get wider and taller handlebars and 7.9-gallon fuel tanks rather than the Pro bikes' 5.3-gallon units. Got all that? Essentially, they're the same chassis, engine, and suspension across all models, but the Rally bikes get some dirt features, and Explorer bikes get the right gear for long tours. All four get Bosch radar front and rear, as well, to enable both adaptive cruise control and rear close-follow warnings — they're all competent tourers, big tank or no. The best change for 2027 to my eye, though, is the appearance of the new Tiger 1200 lineup. The prior bikes were stuck in an awkward in-between period, where Triumph was in the process of ditching its long-lasting twin-headlight design but hadn't yet gone all-in on compact LED illumination. Now it has, and the Tiger looks all the better for it — that single center headlight below the light bar really works for me. It's functional, too, with corner lighting built into the central LED that illuminates when the rider leans.

title: GS Entec's Ulsan Plant: Asia's Largest Offshore Wind Hub - 조선일보
content: 300 Billion Won Facility Automates Monopile Production for 15MW Turbines, Secures Major Contracts GS Group is accelerating its expansion into the eco-friendly energy ecosystem. The company has transformed GS Entec, which previously manufactured large-scale equipment for GS Caltex and other petrochemical plants, into Asia’s largest production hub for offshore wind turbine foundations. GS Entec held a completion ceremony on October 26 at its Ulsan Yongjam Plant for a 300 billion Korean won automated production facility dedicated to monopiles. Monopiles are massive steel pillars driven into the seabed to support offshore wind turbines. The event was attended by GS Group Chairman Huh Tae-soo, GS Co., Ltd. Vice Chairman Hong Soon-ki, GS Entec CEO Huh Chul-hong, and Koen Bogers, CEO of Dutch partner Sif. Chairman Huh has shown particular interest in the business transition, reportedly visiting the site multiple times to monitor progress. GS Entec has long produced ultra-large chemical equipment, including pressure vessels and heat exchangers for petrochemical plants. However, as global carbon neutrality efforts slowed traditional petrochemical plant orders, the company had to revise its survival strategy. GS Group and GS Entec found a solution in technological continuity: the precision machining and welding of thick steel plates required for petrochemical pressure vessels closely resemble the processes needed for monopile production. Partnering with Sif, the world’s top monopile manufacturer, GS Entec began overhauling its Ulsan factory in October 2024, automating key processes. With an annual production capacity of 150,000 tons, the facility is Asia’s first and largest capable of producing monopiles for 15MW-class offshore wind turbines. It has already secured contracts to supply 64 monopiles worth 200 billion Korean won for the Yeonggwang Nakwol Offshore Wind Project (365MW) and 37 large monopiles for the Taean Offshore Wind Project. Leveraging this track record, GS Entec plans to aggressively target markets in Japan and other parts of Asia.

title: GS Entec Opens Asia's Largest Monopile Plant in Ulsan - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Ulsan Yongjam Plant Completed
Preheating Under Way to Weld 34-Meter Steel Cylinders
Annual Monopile Capacity Expanded to 150,000 Tons
300 Billion Won Invested in Asia's Largest Base
Targeting Nine Offshore Wind Projects in Korea and Japan ULSAN — At GS Entec's Yongjam plant in Ulsan on the 26th, more than a dozen small flames burned steadily beneath a massive steel cylinder measuring 34 meters long and weighing 100 tons. The flames were preheating the seams of the steel plate to above 100 degrees Celsius, a step that prepares the welding of "cans," the core components of monopiles, the structures that hold offshore wind turbines in place on the seabed. Welded together with precision, the giant cans form a monopile weighing as much as 2,500 tons. The unit being fabricated at the site that day was a prototype of monopiles to be supplied to the Taean offshore wind power project starting in July next year. The Yongjam plant is Asia's largest production base dedicated to monopiles. GS Entec invested about 300 billion won ($209 million) and began building the production line in October 2024, holding a completion ceremony on the 26th to mark the end of the expansion. The plant's annual monopile capacity has jumped to 150,000 tons from 40,000 tons. The newly operating line incorporates the technology and latest process expertise of Sif, the Netherlands-based company that ranks first globally in monopiles. Engineers on the ground, however, are confident they can surpass Sif. "The core of monopile manufacturing is welding, and our existing chemical equipment business was also based on welding large steel plates," GS Entec CEO Song Won-gil said. "If we secure enough time to master the equipment, we can catch up with Sif. Sif officials who visited the plant and watched our manufacturing process told us they respect us." On the strength of that capacity, GS Entec aims to win nine offshore wind projects in South Korea and Japan by 2030. The company signed a contract in 2023 to supply 64 monopiles worth about 200 billion won ($139 million) to the Yeonggwang Nakwol offshore wind farm (365 megawatts) and completed installation of all units in June this year, demonstrating its ability to execute projects from fabrication through delivery. Last month it also won the right to supply 37 monopiles for the Taean offshore wind power project (504 megawatts). The company is targeting annual revenue of 350 billion to 400 billion won. GS Group Chairman Huh Tae-soo also visited the ceremony to lend support. "It carries symbolic meaning in that we transformed existing chemical equipment manufacturing facilities into renewable energy infrastructure, turning the shift toward energy transition into a business opportunity and achieving an active business transformation," Huh said. "It is an important case showing that GS Group is expanding into future growth areas including AI data centers, renewable energy and related infrastructure." GS Entec CEO Huh Chul-hong said the company would "combine Sif's technology with GS Entec's manufacturing capabilities to strengthen competitiveness in quality and delivery, and expand our position in the global offshore wind market on the basis of our domestic track record." Voices at the site, however, said building dedicated monopile quays is urgently needed if South Korea's offshore wind industry is to become globally competitive. Installing offshore wind substructures depends heavily on rough maritime weather, leaving only about 90 days a year when work is actually possible. That is why storage yards and dedicated quays that allow immediate shipment to sea when weather permits are essential. "We are temporarily using Mokpo Port and Mokpo New Port, but there is not enough space to store monopiles weighing 1,650 tons," Song said. "Offshore wind powerhouses such as the United States, Denmark and Germany have large dedicated quays spanning more than 200,000 pyeong. If the government leads the development of such quays, we can participate in funds to raise the competitiveness of Korea's offshore wind industry." title: GS Entec pivots to offshore wind, invests 300b won to expand Korea capacity - Chosunbiz
content: Ulsan plant overhaul quadruples monopile output as GS Entec eyes Japanese orders and seeks stronger port backing A cylindrical steel structure "can" with a diameter of 10 m and a thickness of 90 mm was neatly placed on advanced automated production equipment. Welders poured dozens of steady sparks from two points inside and four outside. The precise welding work to join giant steel plates was being carried out without human hands. After repeatedly welding along the circumference of a "section" formed by joining cans, a 10-step process of coating and shipping meshed like an organism within a 250,000㎡ site. ◇ Dedicated monopile plant after 2 years…production capacity expanded by about fourfold The "dedicated monopile production facility completion ceremony" held on the 26th at GS Entec's Ulsan Yongjam Plant was not merely an event to announce the completion of facilities. GS Group Chairman Huh Tae-soo said it "is meaningful" in that the company seized the era's shift to energy transition as a new business opportunity and achieved a proactive business pivot. Technical cooperation partner Sif CEO Coon Voghers of the Netherlands also said it is "a starting point" for GS Entec to continuously contribute to the energy transition on which future generations' lives depend. A monopile is a cylindrical steel structure that supports an offshore wind turbine from the seabed. Until just two years ago, this plant produced refining and petrochemical equipment. But as the petrochemical industry suffered from oversupply and the offshore wind market expanded with countries' carbon neutrality policies, GS Entec also had to find a new growth engine. That is why GS Entec decided in Jul. 2024 to invest 300 billion won to convert its production facilities. It was a choice to change the very constitution of the company, beyond simply switching product lines. With this conversion, GS Entec greatly increased its annual monopile production capacity from 40,000 tons to 150,000 tons. It can manufacture ultra-large monopiles with a maximum diameter of 11 m, steel plate thickness of 160 mm, length of 100 m, and weight of 2,500 tons. It also produces products used in 15 MW-class large offshore wind turbines. It applied steel plate processing and welding technologies accumulated in the refining and petrochemical equipment manufacturing process to the offshore wind sector and built automated facilities to improve production efficiency. ◇ After Yeonggwang-Nakwol, wins 37 units for Taean, targets Japan market Orders are piling up. In the Jeonnam Yeonggwang-Nakwol offshore wind project, GS Entec won an order for 64 monopiles worth about 200 billion won and completed installation by Jun. this year. Last month, it signed a contract to supply 37 monopiles for the 504 MW Taean Offshore Wind project to be built off the coast of Taean, South Chungcheong. The supply volume is 51,000 tons, about 34% of annual production capacity. Deliveries will be made sequentially from Jul. next year to Aug. 2028. GS Entec plans to expand its sales channels from domestic offshore wind projects to overseas markets, including Japan, Asia, and Australia. Park Ki-yeol, GS Entec's sales and order management team leader, said, "We are aiming to win two to three projects in Korea and one to two in Japan." In particular, it plans to expand orders in line with capacity, focusing on nine projects expected to be tendered from mid-2028 to 2030. ◇ Tasks in port infrastructure amid low-priced push from China…government support is key The key is government support for industrial infrastructure. Japan has designated seven hub ports that support assembly and installation of offshore wind equipment and is refurbishing the piers. The United Kingdom also said in Jan. this year that it had induced 3.4 billion pounds (about 6 trillion won) in private investment by injecting 204 million pounds (about 360 billion won) in public funds into manufacturing facilities and ports. China's price offensive is also fierce. According to energy market research firm Rystad Energy, China's monopile manufacturing cost is about 41% lower than Europe's. Price competition pressure is growing on our corporations as well. Domestically, securing port infrastructure is cited as a task no less important than production facilities. Co-CEO Song Won-gil of GS Entec said, "Because of offshore weather conditions, the number of days when actual monopile installation work is possible is about 90 days a year," and noted, "We need a dedicated logistics hub that can store pre-made monopiles and supply them immediately when conditions allow installation." The ground bearing capacity of general piers is about 5 tons per ㎡, but to handle ultra-large monopiles, they must withstand 30 tons or more per ㎡. GS Entec is currently utilizing existing facilities such as Mokpo New Port, Mokpo Daebul Industrial Complex, and Ulsan Port. There is no immediate disruption to production, but the position is that a separate logistics base is needed to store and transport large volumes stably. CEO Song said, "If the government takes the lead in preparing related facilities, corporations can also participate in funds or endowments and make use of them." In Jul., the government announced a plan to expand eight berths for offshore wind support piers at five ports—Mokpo, Gunsan, Incheon, Ulsan, and Taean. However, as they are being pursued for various purposes such as assembly, installation, and maintenance of power generation equipment, it is unclear whether they will meet the shipping demand of monopile manufacturers. Observers say that for the expansion of production facilities to translate into export competitiveness, port support that takes into account conditions for storing and loading ultra-large equipment is needed. In practice, tasks such as consultations among relevant ministries and compensation for fishing rights remain before pier expansion can proceed. An official of the National Assembly's Committee on Climate, Energy, Environment and Labor said, "The expansion of offshore wind support piers is not a matter decided by an announcement from the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries alone, and requires consultations with local governments and the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment," and added, "Because there are compensation issues for fishing rights and customary fishing, we will consult at the standing committee level to ensure local governments push ahead with commitment." A key government official also said, "As the president has stressed that 'the nation's fate depends on the transition of the energy system,' this is a task that must move faster," and noted, "Consultations are currently underway among relevant ministries." title: GS Entec Transforms Ulsan Factory into Offshore Wind Base - 조선일보
content: Investing 300 Billion Won, GS Entec Automates Monopile Production for 15MW Turbines with Sif GS Entec, which has produced equipment for oil refining and petrochemical plants, has invested 300 billion Korean won to transform its Ulsan factory into a specialized production base for offshore wind turbine substructures. Leveraging its 30 years of accumulated technology in manufacturing large-scale steel equipment, the company has made a leap from the traditional 'smokestack industry' to the eco-friendly energy sector. On October 26, GS Entec held a completion ceremony for its 'Monopile (Monopile) dedicated automated production facility' at its Yongjam factory in Ulsan. The event was attended by Huh Tae-soo, GS Group chairman; Hong Soon-ki, GS vice chairman; Huh Chul-hong, CEO of GS Entec; and Koen Bogers, CEO of Dutch company Sif, among others. A monopile is a massive steel pillar driven into the seabed to support offshore wind turbines. GS Entec partnered with Sif, the world's top monopile manufacturer, and began a full-scale renovation of its Ulsan factory in October 2024, automating many core processes. With an annual production capacity of 150,000 tons, the facility is Asia's first and largest capable of producing monopiles to support ultra-large wind turbines rated at 15MW (megawatts). Huh Tae-soo, GS Group chairman, stated, "The completion of this facility, which transformed a chemical equipment factory into a renewable energy production site, is a symbolic example of seizing energy transition as a new business opportunity." He added, "It demonstrates GS Group's expansion into future growth areas such as AI data centers and renewable energy infrastructure." It was reported that Chairman Huh paid special attention to the factory conversion, visiting the site multiple times during the process. ◇ Factory that made chemical equipment for 30 years switches to offshore wind power Established in 1988, GS Entec is a subsidiary of GS Global. The company has achieved stable performance by manufacturing large-scale chemical equipment, including pressure vessels and reactors for oil refining and petrochemical plants. However, as global carbon neutrality trends slowed orders for traditional oil refining and petrochemical plants, revising its survival strategy became inevitable. GS Group and GS Entec found the answer in technological continuity. They recognized that the technology for manufacturing pressure vessels for oil refineries and monopiles shares similarities in precisely processing and welding thick steel plates. As offshore wind turbines have grown larger, reaching 10-15MW, monopiles are also trending toward larger diameters and heavier weights. The companies believed that leveraging GS Entec's steel manufacturing technology would secure competitiveness. During a visit on October 26, the Yongjam factory in Ulsan was in the process of trial-producing monopiles. The expansive factory, covering a total site area of 250,000 square meters, was designed to allow massive steel plates and processed components to move along the production line via conveyor belts, large grippers, and lifts. To create a monopile, steel plates weighing approximately 20 tons each are first welded together to form a 30-meter-long plate. The edges are then precision-finished to within ±0.5mm tolerance. The plate is rolled into a cylindrical shape using a large bending machine. Welding the ends of the rolled plate creates a massive ring-shaped 'can.' The factory can produce cans with a diameter of 11 meters and a steel plate thickness of 160mm. Multiple cans are precisely welded together to form a steel pillar for offshore wind turbines, measuring 100 meters in length and weighing 2,500 tons. The automation of key processes—from steel plate processing to cylindrical forming, welding, and assembly—is a hallmark of the Yongjam factory. Order achievements are already emerging. Before the factory conversion, in 2023, GS Entec secured an order worth approximately 200 billion Korean won for 64 monopiles measuring 7.5 meters in diameter and 71 meters in length for the Yeonggwang Nakwol Offshore Wind Project, 365MW, completing installation last June. In September, the company additionally won a contract to supply 37 monopiles for the Taean Offshore Wind Project, 504MW. These are large products with a diameter of approximately 10.6 meters and a length of approximately 80 meters. The offshore wind market is also expected to expand. The government announced a mid- to long-term bidding roadmap for offshore wind in June, planning to put a total of 55GW-scale projects up for competitive bidding over 10 years until 2035. GS Entec plans to use its domestic order achievements as a foothold to target the Asian market, including Japan.

title: Goldman or Morgan Stanley: Which Stock Is Better Bet Post Q3 Results? - The Globe and Mail
content: Wall Street heavyweights The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.GS and Morgan StanleyMS continue to capitalize on improving investment banking (IB) activity, robust equities trading and growing demand for financial services. Both companies delivered impressive third-quarter 2026 results, reflecting their strong market positions and ability to navigate a dynamic operating environment. The continued recovery in mergers and acquisitions (M&As), healthy underwriting activity, and strong institutional client engagement have supported their financial performances. While Goldman has demonstrated stronger IB revenue growth and trading momentum, Morgan Stanley continues to benefit from its diversified business model and expanding wealth management franchise. Against this backdrop, which IB powerhouse offers better investment prospects following the latest quarterly results? Let us examine. Goldman remains a dominant player in M&A advisory, underwriting and trading. The company's IB business has benefited significantly from improving global dealmaking activity and capital markets issuance. During the first nine months of 2026, IB fees jumped 40% year over year to $9.46 billion, supported by increases of 34%, 73% and 29% in advisory, equity underwriting and debt underwriting revenues, respectively. Management continues to view the capital markets environment favorably, with opportunities arising from strategic dealmaking, technology investments and AI infrastructure financing. Although higher interest rates and macroeconomic uncertainties could affect deal activity, GS's leading market position and healthy pipeline position it well to capitalize on the ongoing investment banking recovery. Goldman continues to streamline its operations by exiting non-core consumer banking businesses and strengthening its core franchises. The company is accelerating expansion in asset and wealth management to diversify its revenue sources and generate more durable fee-based income. In sync with these efforts, in August 2026, Goldman announced an agreement to acquire NEOS Investments, a provider of derivative income exchange-traded funds (ETFs). In April 2026, Goldman completed the acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, expanding its active exchange-traded fund (ETF) capabilities. Earlier, it completed the acquisition of Industry Ventures to strengthen its presence in venture capital and alternative investments. These initiatives complement its efforts to expand private market offerings and deepen client relationships. The benefits of Goldman's strategic repositioning are increasingly evident in its financial performance. For the first nine months of 2026, GBM revenues jumped 34% to $41.72 billion, while AWM revenues rose 15% to $13.73 billion. Continued asset gathering and strategic acquisitions should support recurring fee income and reduce the dependence on market-sensitive businesses over time. Morgan Stanley continues to leverage its integrated business model, encompassing institutional securities, wealth management and investment management. The company has strategically diversified its revenue streams to reduce the dependence on volatile capital markets activities while benefiting from improving IB conditions. The company's IB performance remained strong during the first nine months of 2026, with consolidated IB revenues increasing 30% year over year to $7.30 billion. The company is well-positioned to benefit from a healthier deal environment, supported by a robust and diversified pipeline across regions and sectors. Momentum is expanding beyond the Americas into Asia and EMEA, while active M&A and IPO markets, together with the company’s strong competitive position, are expected to support further growth as the macroeconomic backdrop evolves. Morgan Stanley's strategic focus on expanding wealth and investment management operations remains a major strength. Acquisitions such as E*TRADE and Eaton Vance have enhanced its scale and diversified its business mix. Further, the acquisition of EquityZen, completed in January 2026, strengthened its private markets capabilities and offerings for corporate and wealth management clients. The benefits of this transformation were evident in the first nine months of 2026. Wealth Management revenues increased 13.4% year over year to $26.44 billion. Moreover, the business attracted $498.9 billion in net new assets and $173.3 billion in fee-based asset flows during the first nine months of 2026. Wealth Management client assets reached $8.43 trillion as of September-end, up 19.5% year over year, while combined client assets across Wealth and Investment Management stood at $10.5 trillion, highlighting the growing scale of Morgan Stanley's wealth management franchise. This expanding client asset base provides Morgan Stanley with significant opportunities to generate recurring fee revenues and deepen client engagement. Over the past year, Goldman shares have gained 10.9%, outperforming Morgan Stanley’s 8.1% rise. In comparison, the industry has returned 3.3%. From a valuation perspective, Goldman appears relatively attractive. Its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio stands at 11.94X, below Morgan Stanley's 13.56X. title: Longview business works with outreach mission to give bikes to employed people in need - Longview News-Journal
content: A partnership between a Longview shop and a homeless outreach mission is providing bicycles to people who need a mode of transportation to get to work. For the past month, Woolley G’s Bike and Fitness has refurbished bicycles and given them to Newgate Mission’s “Bike to Work” program. While Newgate primarily serves the city’s homeless community, the program is open to anyone needing a mode of transportation to get to work. The program is simple: People donate used but repairable bikes to Woolley G’s. Woolley G’s employees fix and donate them to Newgate. Newgate staffers then distribute them to people who need them. “We just thought that was a good opportunity,” said Gary Ford, a partner at Woolley G’s. “We get some that are in pretty good shape, and so it doesn’t take a lot to get them running.” In the past month, Woolley G’s employees have repaired five bikes for the program, Ford said. He dropped off two bikes at Newgate this past week. People who want to donate a bike to the program can bring it to Woolley G’s, 306 E Tyler St., each week from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Friday and 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Saturday. People are encouraged to donate lightly used bikes rather than bikes that need serious, costly repairs. “If it’s not shifting well, not braking well, maybe needs some new tires or some new grips — that’s something that we can do inexpensively out of our own pocket,” he said. Woolley G’s is absorbing the cost of employee labor and minor repairs as part of the program, Ford said. Some community members are donating to Newgate to cover the cost of more significant repairs and to help repair bikes that people already have. Helping people who need a mode of transportation is rewarding, Ford said. “Not everybody can afford a car,” he said. “Bicycles are a cheap and expensive way to get around.” Jeanette Pleasant, an administrator at Newgate, said the program is helping people get to and from their jobs and government offices such as the Social Security Administration. “Most of them are off the street, homeless people,” she said. “We just try to help them and do as much as we can.” The program is open to anyone in need, not just Newgate clients, she said. “They can be somebody that just came in off the street or walked up here and needed a bike,” she said. “I just interview them, and if everything checks out for them, I give them a bike.” Newgate Mission is along Mobberly Avenue, where a bike lane was built as part of a “complete street” road renovation project. City leaders plan to build more bike lanes and sidewalks in the future to improve transportation for bicyclists and pedestrians alike. Those projects — and programs such as the Bike to Work program — will help people without cars get to work, grocery stores and more, Ford said. “If you’ve got a bike that’s kind of collecting dust in your garage, we’d love to get it in the hands of somebody that could use it,” he said.
